text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) board is concerned that a possible extension of 115 billion levs required from the finance ministry for the second revision of the 1996 budget may increase the risk of hyperinflation, BNB governor Lyubomir Filipov said.
-- The state owned United Bulgarian Bank raised its capital to 21.07 billion levs from 679.5 million levs.
-- Deputy Prime Minister Roumen Gechev discussed the possible introduction of a currency board with representatives of six leading state banks.

-- Bulgaria is expecting to receive the report of a British company evaluating the concession sought by Bulgarian-Russian gas joint stock company Topenergy for transiting Russian gas through Bulgaria's territory, an Energy ministry official said.
-- The central bank will present today the new 10,000 lev note which is expected to be put in circulation in the next few days.
-- Bulgarian costoms officers said they had seized 45 kg of heroin hidden in a passenger bus owned by a Bulgarian private company on the Kalotina border checkpoint with Yugoslavia.
-- Bulgaria will cut some 50,000 jobs in the public sector if a currency board system is introduced in the country, Social Minister Mincho Koralski said.

-- Bulgaria's biggest trade union organisation, the Confederation of Independent Trade Unions, said some 886,000 workers joined Wednesday's strike to demand a government reshuffle and early parliamentary elections.
-- Bulgarian State Railways (BSR) will not raise passenger ticket prices again until March 1, a BSR senior official said. BSR raised passenger ticket prices by 30 percent on December 1.

-- Bulgaria's commercial banks are stimulating the fall of the lev as they are still holding long foreign currency positions and not selling currency to their big clients despite the memorandum signed with the central bank in July and a gentlemen's agreement reached in November, the head of BNB's forex operations department Dimitar Murdgov said.

-- South Korean Daewoo Corp plans large scale investment in Bulgaria as it is interested in buying the state fertiliser producer Himko-Vratsa, the state forklift truck producer Balkankar Holding, the state Balkanbank and Efir 2 channel of Bulgaria's National Television, a Daewoo senior official said.
